title: CaRe High TG – A non-interventional registry study to collect real-world data from patients with severe hypertriglyceridaemia (sHTG)
summary: CaRe High TG is a German research project investigating people with persistently high triglyceride levels (severe dyslipidaemia). The aim is to gain a better understanding of the causes and risk factors of the condition, as well as potential complications such as pancreatitis and cardiovascular disease. The project is also investigating how the condition develops over time and what impact lifestyle changes and various treatment options have on the health and quality of life of those affected. Participants regularly complete digital questionnaires via an online platform or, preferably, the CaRe High app. The aim is to determine how regular monitoring of blood lipid levels and general health affects well-being and how the condition is managed in everyday life.
conditions: Familial chylomicronemia syndrome, multifactorial chylomicronemia syndrome, type III hyperlipoproteinaemia, combined hyperlipoproteinaemia

interventions.name:
Patients with sHTG complete a monthly digital ‘event diary’.
Participating doctors complete a questionnaire at baseline, as well as annual follow-up questionnaires. For patients being treated with ApoC3-ASOs, quarterly follow-ups will take place, where feasible within the context of routine clinica

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
Adult patients may be included in the study if they meet the following criteria:
1. An FCS score of 7 or higher OR a single fasting TG level > 20 mmol/l (1770 mg/dl) OR three consecutive fasting TG levels > 10 mmol/l (885 mg/dl)
AND
2. A genetic panel test for HTG has been carried out (regardless of the result)
AND
3. Conventional lipid-lowering therapy OR therapy with ApoC3 ASOs
Exclusion criteria:
- individuals under the age of 18;
- individuals who refuse to give written consent to participate;
- individuals who show clinically evident impairment of their cognitive functions;
- individuals who are unable to understand the purpose of the project; and
- individuals who have been diagnosed with decompensated, acute psychiatric disorders.
